mcqs.q: Which test had the highest ability to correctly diagnose dermatophytosis in this study?
mcqs.e: ATI was positive in 100% (20/20), outperforming Wood's lamp and the trichogram.

mcqs.q: Which dermatophyte was most frequently isolated on fungal culture?
mcqs.e: M. canis accounted for 16 of the isolates, far more than the others.

mcqs.q: Compared with the trichogram, the ATI detected fungal elements in >20 HPF:
mcqs.e: Fungal elements were seen in >20 HPF more often with ATI (18/20) than trichogram (11/20).

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about terbinafine for feline sporotrichosis?
o: It is curative in most cats
It is not an effective treatment option
It eliminates the need for follow-up
mcqs.e: The low clinical-cure rate indicated terbinafine is not an effective option.

mcqs.q: Of the 30 cats completing follow-up, how many achieved clinical cure?
mcqs.e: Only 10/30 were cured; treatment failed in 18 and 2 died.

mcqs.q: Which adverse effect was commonly observed with terbinafine?
mcqs.e: Adverse reactions were frequent, with 10 cats showing elevated transaminases.

mcqs.q: How did the in-clinic ELISA perform for detecting CPV antibodies in adult vaccinated bitches?
mcqs.e: Both ELISA and HI showed all 16 bitches had protective titers, confirming ELISA reliability in adults.

mcqs.q: For protective maternally-derived antibody titers in unvaccinated puppies, which assay yielded the lower positive percentage?
mcqs.e: HI detected protective MDA in 91.9% vs only 40.4% by ELISA.

mcqs.q: The authors suggest the in-clinic ELISA may be useful to:
o: Predict the best time to vaccinate puppies
mcqs.e: ELISA's declining MDA detection could help time puppy vaccination and reduce failures.

mcqs.q: What survival rate was achieved with in-hospital treatment of canine parvoviral enteritis?
mcqs.e: 294 of 322 dogs (91%) survived.

mcqs.q: Which presentation finding was a negative prognostic indicator for survival?
mcqs.e: A low HCT was associated with markedly lower odds of survival.

mcqs.q: Increased total serum magnesium at presentation was associated with:
mcqs.e: Each 0.1 mmol/L rise in magnesium conferred 2.5 lower odds of survival.

mcqs.q: What was the key finding regarding the FPV-like virus isolated from dogs?
o: It is identical to vaccine CPV-2
mcqs.e: The study confirmed FPV-like isolates efficiently infect dogs and circulate in China.

mcqs.q: Phylogenetically, the 6 isolated FPV-like strains were most closely related to:
mcqs.e: Genome, VP2 and NS1 trees placed them with FPV rather than CPV-2.

mcqs.q: Approximately what proportion of Carnivore protoparvovirus 1-positive samples were FPV-like?
mcqs.e: 28 of 113 (24.8%) positive strains were FPV-like.

mcqs.q: How did serum cobalamin in CPV-infected dogs compare with healthy controls?
mcqs.e: Cobalamin was significantly lower in CPV-infected dogs (median 173 vs 379 pmol/L).

mcqs.q: What was the relationship between cobalamin and CRP or albumin concentrations?
mcqs.e: No association was found between cobalamin and either CRP or albumin.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about the hypocobalaminemia found?
o: Common but clinical relevance remains undetermined
mcqs.e: Hypocobalaminemia was common but its clinical relevance remains to be determined.

mcqs.q: Which sampling site had the lowest qRT-PCR sensitivity in sick dogs?
mcqs.e: Fecal samples had the lowest sensitivity in clinically ill dogs.

mcqs.q: What hampered the specificity of molecular CPV detection?
o: Temporary positivity during the post-vaccination period
mcqs.e: Recently vaccinated dogs transiently shed vaccine virus, temporarily reducing specificity.

mcqs.q: Which sampling sites were deemed suitable for CPV qRT-PCR?
mcqs.e: All three sites (blood, feces, pharynx) were suitable for detection.

mcqs.q: The FPV-DL04 strain isolated from cats in Dalian was characterized as:
mcqs.e: Despite the FPV-DL04 name, it was identified as a novel CPV-2c strain.

mcqs.q: The FPV-DL04 strain showed highest homology (99.4%) with which strain?
mcqs.e: It shared 99.4% homology with the CPV-2c CN/HN1708 strain.

mcqs.q: Which key mutation sites were present in the DL04 strain?
mcqs.e: DL04 carried S297A and A300G but lacked F267Y and Y324I.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of early CPMA treatment on CPV-2-induced mortality?
o: Prevented mortality in all treated dogs
mcqs.e: Mortality was prevented in all CPMA-treated dogs versus 57% in controls.

mcqs.q: Did CPMA treatment after infection interfere with adaptive immunity?
mcqs.e: Both groups showed similar IgM responses, so CPMA did not impair adaptive immunity.

mcqs.q: What was the mortality rate in the saline control group?
mcqs.e: Controls had 57% mortality compared with none in treated dogs.

mcqs.q: How did the immunogenicity of the 0.5 ml feline vaccine compare with the 1 ml version?
mcqs.e: The reduced-volume vaccine kept the same immunogenicity as the 1 ml product.

mcqs.q: What was observed regarding local adverse events with the reduced-volume vaccine?
mcqs.e: The 0.5 ml vaccine was well tolerated and induced fewer local events.

mcqs.q: Which antigens did the reduced-volume vaccine contain?
o: Feline herpesvirus, calicivirus, panleukopenia and leukemia
mcqs.e: It was a non-adjuvanted FHV/FCV/panleukopenia/FeLV vaccine.

mcqs.q: Where did most FPV evolution occur according to the phylodynamic analysis?
mcqs.e: Few long-distance introductions occurred; most evolution was local.

mcqs.q: What was the FPV population-size trend over time?
mcqs.e: FPV showed constant size until a more recent expansion beginning around 2000.

mcqs.q: What was the relationship between viral phylogeny and disease severity?
o: Apparent influence without strong statistical association
mcqs.e: Several clinical variables appeared phylogeny-influenced but without strong statistical significance.

mcqs.q: Did asymptomatic intestinal parasites significantly affect the FPV vaccine antibody response in kittens?
mcqs.e: Vaccination response did not differ significantly between kittens with and without parasites (P = 0.13).

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about postponing vaccination because of intestinal parasitism?
o: Parasitism is not a reason to postpone vaccination
Deworming must always precede the first dose
mcqs.e: Asymptomatic endoparasitism did not interfere with response, so it should not delay vaccination.

mcqs.q: Which intestinal parasite was most commonly identified in the affected kittens?
mcqs.e: Toxocara cati (12/17) was the most common parasite found.
